name: Hochzeiger Bergbahnen
kurzbeschreibung: The Hochzeiger Bergbahnen in Jerzens in the Pitztal Valley access a family alpine paradise up to 2,560 m, home to the award-winning Stone Pine Park and mountain carts.
preis: Hiking paths freely accessible; gondola tickets and ZirbenCart mountain cart rentals apply fees
oeffnungszeiten: Summer cable car operations daily from early June to mid-October
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Hochzeiger Bergbahnen cable car network, based in the village of Jerzens in the front Pitztal Valley, unlocks an expansive and sun-blessed alpine playground reaching up to 2,560 metres above sea level. Cradled by the dramatic crests of the Ötztal Alps, the Hochzeiger ranks among the premier summer excursion and hiking mountains in Western Austria. The region is internationally celebrated for its ancient, fragrant stone pine (Zirbe) woodlands, which represent one of the largest contiguous Swiss pine forests in the Northern Alps. Right at the mid-station at an elevation of 2,000 metres lies the acclaimed 'ZirbenPark': across an interactive discovery trail, children and adults explore the lore of the 'Queen of the Alps', climb a 12-metre-tall stone pine cone observation tower, and whiz down giant tube slides. Modern gondolas and chairlifts carry visitors swiftly into high-alpine terrain with vistas stretching towards the Zugspitze.

Route & Anforderungen

The Hochzeiger trail system spans over 100 kilometres of signposted mountain tracks catering to every fitness level. The one-kilometre nature loop within the ZirbenPark at the mid-station is entirely barrier-free, level, and well suited for all-terrain strollers (approx. one hour stroll). Adventure seekers can rent a three-wheeled off-road mountain cart ('ZirbenCart') at the Seppelbahn top terminal and cruise down a dedicated, safety-engineered 3.7-kilometre alpine track to the mid-station. Mountain hikers can ascend from the mid-station via the Sechszeiger ridge (2,395 m) to the main Hochzeiger summit cross at 2,560 metres (approx. 2 hours walk, 560 metres ascent). Standard sneakers suffice around the mid-station, whereas ankle-high trekking boots with rubber lugged soles are mandatory for summits.

Besuch & Anreise

Motorists travel via motorway A12 (exit Imst/Pitztal) and follow provincial road L16 through the Pitztal Valley via Wenns up to Jerzens. The mountain road leads directly to the lift base in Liss (Jerzens), where abundant complimentary parking is provided. Rail travelers arrive at Imst-Pitztal station and board synchronized regional VVT postbuses directly to the lift base.

Tipps

Take time to savor authentic stone-pine culinary specialties on the sun terrace of the Zeigerrestaurant at the mid-station, including regional Tyrolean dumplings and artisan Zirbenschnaps liqueur. Renting a ZirbenCart for the downhill ride is guaranteed fun for kids and teenagers alike.
